title: Powdery mildew fungal disease in sunflower

Header: Powdery mildew fungal disease in sunflower
Golovinomyces cichoracearum ( syn. Erysiphe cichoracearum ) Ubwiri poda in Swahili

Prevention: A strong healthy sunflower crop tolerates the disease.
Maintain plant density of about 1 metre around each plant.
Plant early at beginning of rainy seasons to escape the main disease period.
Deep bury or plough under crop residues after harvesting, because they host mildew spores.
However, if no major insect pests and diseases are in your crop, then do not plough to avoid water evaporation.
Break cropping of sunflowers for 2-3 years after heavy mildew infestation.
Rotate with non susceptible crops such as cereals.
Monitoring: This is a fungal disease which affects leaves starting from the older lower leaves upward.
Stem and heads may be affected later.
Visit field every two weeks after crop emergence.
Look for whitish roundish areas (fungal colonies) on upper side of leaves.
Consider chemical spray, when fungal colonies are present on 3-4 out of 10 plants or when neighbouring farms are infested.
Early action is needed as most fungicides are protectants, not curative.
Act earlier if plants are stressed (such as drought, poor soils, etc.), because strong plants can tolerate mildew.
Do not act on fully grown or ripening sunflowers as action is too late.
Direct Control: Remove and bury all infested leaves/plants deeply up to 50 centimetres.
Bupirimate-based products (usually at 250g/ litre, but double check product label).
Sulphur products (Sulphur, Kumulus, Sulgro, ThiovitJet, Salfa, and others).
Restrictions: The following products are protectants, thus they may prevent further spread, and only moderately suppress already established mildew fungi.

When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval, max number of sprays, restricted re-entry interval.
Do not empty into drains and water sources.
